```js
app.use(cors({ origin: true, credentials: true }));
```
`origin: true` reflects the request's Origin header back, and `credentials: true` allows cookies. This means ANY origin can make credentialed (cookie-authenticated) cross-origin requests to the API. This is a real exploitable CSRF/credential-theft issue if the API uses cookie-based auth. This is exploitable. Combined with `req.user.settings` being used in preferences (suggesting authenticated sessions), credentialed CORS from any origin is dangerous.

This is a HIGH severity finding (effectively disables same-origin credential protection).

cookieSecure: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production'

const TRUSTED = new Set(['10.0.0.10','10.0.0.11']);
function trustProxy(address) { return TRUSTED.has(address); }

This trusts only specific IPs as proxies. This is actually a GOOD implementation (explicit allowlist), not a vulnerability. Many apps mistakenly trust all. So not a finding.
